chunk_findings.detail: With `gates.scrub_secret_names = "on"` — the knob’s declared `strictest` value — and the default `secret_name_patterns`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` matches `_API_KEY` and is removed from the gate/CI child environment. Project rule [r-gemini-key-load] requires the Gemini reviewer key to be exported into the child before a review, because otherwise the gemini reviewer sends no key and requests fail. Thus the “strictest” recommendation encourages a configuration that breaks required gemini reviews unless the operator also manually adds `GEMINI_API_KEY` to `keep_env`; the knob should exempt required `api_key_env` variables or make that requirement explicit.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/config_sections/gates.py` `scrub_secret_names`

chunk_findings.detail: The doctor note claims that setting `gates.scrub_secret_names = "on"` removes the listed names from “every gate and CI child” and mentions only `[gates].keep_env` as an exception. But `[ci].keep_env` also preserves variables in CI children. For example, with `secret_name_patterns = ["TOKEN"]`, `ci.keep_env = ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]`, and a non-CI gate run that recorded `env_secret_mode = "warn"` and `env_secret_names = ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]`, `doctor_notes` emits the note. If the operator follows it and sets scrubbing on, `child_env(..., ci=True)` will still preserve `GITHUB_TOKEN` because `[ci].keep_env` is consulted, so the note’s “CI child” claim is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gateenv.py:doctor_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The documented per-run override `DDFLOW_GATES_SCRUB_SECRET_NAMES=on` contains the default secret-name fragment `_SECRET` (case-blind substring match). Therefore, with the documented default patterns, the scrubber treats its own configuration override as a secret-shaped variable: in `warn` mode the gate evidence/doctor reports `DDFLOW_GATES_SCRUB_SECRET_NAMES` as a secret-shaped name even though it is only a knob setting, and in `on` mode the variable is removed from child environments, so a nested `ddflow`/gate child does not see the per-run setting that enabled scrubbing. The change should exclude ddflow’s own config environment variables (or avoid matching the override variable name) instead of scrubbing/warning the control variable itself.
chunk_findings.title: docs/guide/configuration.md (added `DDFLOW_GATES_SCRUB_SECRET_NAMES` / default `secret_name_patterns`)

chunk_findings.detail: The self-match fix is too broad: it exempts every name beginning with `DDFLOW_`, not just known ddflow configuration overrides. With the default `secret_name_patterns` and `gates.scrub_secret_names = "warn"`, an environment variable such as `DDFLOW_API_KEY= [REDACTED] is filtered out by `not k.upper().startswith(OWN_PREFIX)`, so it is not recorded in `env_secret_names`; with `gates.scrub_secret_names = "on"`, the same variable is not removed from the gate/CI child. `DDFLOW_API_KEY` is secret-shaped by the documented patterns but is not the new knob’s override name, so arbitrary secret-shaped variables in the `DDFLOW_` namespace (or lowercase `ddflow_api_key`, because of `.upper()`) silently bypass the scrubber.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gateenv.py:secret_names

chunk_findings.detail: The fix for the previous `DDFLOW_GATES_SCRUB_SECRET_NAMES` false positive exempts the entire `DDFLOW_*` namespace, so any secret-shaped variable with that prefix is treated as non-secret. The new test proves the behavior: with `cfg.gates.scrub_secret_names = "on"`, `child_env(cfg, base)` keeps `DDFLOW_X_TOKEN` while removing `MY_TOKEN`. If an operator exports, for example, `DDFLOW_X_TOKEN= [REDACTED] (or any `DDFLOW_*_API_KEY`/`DDFLOW_*_TOKEN` value), a gate or CI command run through `shell=True` can still read and print it, and the scrubber neither warns about nor removes it. The previous defect only required exempting actual ddflow configuration override names; a blanket prefix skip creates a name-based bypass for the feature’s stated purpose of removing secret-shaped environment variables from gate/CI children.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_env_secret_shapes.py:test_ddflows_own_settings_are_never_secret_shaped

chunk_findings.detail: The new `DDFLOW_` exemption is name-prefix based, not “recognized ddflow setting” based, so it disables both scrubbing and warning for any secret-shaped variable in that namespace. With the default patterns and `scrub_secret_names=on`, exporting `DDFLOW_MY_API_KEY= [REDACTED] (which matches `_API_KEY` but is not a ddflow setting) leaves the variable in the gate/CI child environment because the prefix check removes it from `secret_named_env`; in `warn` mode it is also absent from `env_secret_names`, so doctor does not note it. A gate command such as `env` can therefore read and print the value despite the knob’s stated behavior that `on` removes variables matching the secret-name patterns.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gateenv.py:secret_named_env

chunk_findings.detail: The new test pins an over-broad prefix exemption: `DDFLOW_X_TOKEN` is asserted to be “never secret-shaped”, even though it is not a documented ddflow setting. The failure scenario is an operator exporting a secret-shaped value under any `DDFLOW_` name, e.g. `DDFLOW_MY_API_KEY= [REDACTED] with `gates.scrub_secret_names = "on"`. Because the implementation treats every `DDFLOW_`-prefixed variable as a ddflow setting, `secret_names` omits it and `child_env` passes it into the gate/CI child; the gate command can then `printenv DDFLOW_MY_API_KEY` and the value can reach the committed log. In `warn` mode the same variable is also omitted from `env_secret_names`, so doctor does not note it. This bypasses the stated purpose of stopping gates from seeing API keys, as also documented in `docs/guide/configuration.md:75`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_env_secret_shapes.py:111
